claims.text: Dynamic formation of oxygenated surface species governs the catalytic activity of PGM nanoscale catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
Dynamic formation of oxygenated surface species governs the selectivity of PGM nanoscale catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
Dynamic formation of oxygenated surface species governs the durability of PGM nanoscale catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
Oxygenated surface species facilitate the 12-electron and 12-proton transfers involved in ethanol oxidation.
The nanoscale size of the catalysts enhances the formation or action of oxygenated surface species.
Nanoscale catalyst size provides increased surface area and reactivity.
Operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations can be used to investigate the dynamic behavior of PGM catalysts during ethanol oxidation.
Introducing operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations will increase catalytic activity by 25% relative to a baseline without those methods.
Introducing operando X-ray absorption spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations will increase selectivity by 15% relative to a baseline without those methods.
Catalytic activity will be measured using ethanol conversion rate.
Catalytic selectivity will be measured using product yield.
The proposed mechanism applies specifically to PGM nanoscale catalysts under ethanol-oxidation conditions and may not generalize to other reaction regimes.
Failure of the characterization-and-calculation condition to produce at least a 10% increase in both activity and selectivity would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Operando spectroscopy and DFT are presented as investigative tools, but the prediction and baseline treat their introduction as a catalyst-modifying intervention that directly raises activity and selectivity. No controlled material or operating change is specified that would alter oxygenated-species formation.

The hypothesis attributes performance to oxygenated species and nanoscale size, whereas the falsification rule tests whether adding measurement and calculation methods increases performance; it does not directly perturb either proposed causal factor.
